name: @oliverames/mcp-server-for-wave

tools.name: wave_auth_status
tools.description: Report how this server resolved its Wave credentials and whether write tools are enabled. Makes no Wave API request, so it works even when the token is missing or expired -- use it first when other tools report authentication problems.

tools.name: wave_get_user
tools.description: Get the Wave user account that owns the current access token. Useful for confirming which account a token authenticates as.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_currencies
tools.description: List the currency codes Wave supports. Wave supports about 160 currencies, so pass search to narrow the list.

search.description: Case-insensitive filter on code or name, e.g. "CAD" or "dollar".

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_get_currency
tools.description: Get one currency by ISO 4217 code.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_countries
tools.description: List the countries Wave supports, with each one's default currency.

search.description: Case-insensitive filter on country code or name.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_get_country
tools.description: Get one country and its provinces or states. Use this to find the province codes that address fields expect.

code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "US", "CA", or "GB".

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_get_province
tools.description: Get one province or state by its code.

code.description: Province code, typically country-qualified, e.g. "CA-ON" or "US-NY".

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_account_types
tools.description: List the five top-level account types in Wave's chart of accounts: ASSET, LIABILITY, EQUITY, INCOME, and EXPENSE, each with its normal balance.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_account_subtypes
tools.description: List account subtypes -- the value wave_create_account needs. Every account belongs to a subtype (CASH_AND_BANK, EXPENSE, INCOME, ...), which in turn determines its type. Some subtypes are system-created and cannot be used for new accounts.

account_type.description: Filter to one type: ASSET, LIABILITY, EQUITY, INCOME, EXPENSE.

creatable_only.description: Exclude system-created subtypes unavailable to new accounts.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_get_oauth_application
tools.description: Get the OAuth application that issued the current access token.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_businesses
tools.description: List the Wave businesses this access token can reach. Start here: every other tool needs a business ID. Pass one to wave_set_default_business so later calls can omit it.

is_archived.description: Filter to archived (true) or active (false) businesses.

fetch_all.description: Walk every page instead of returning just one. Slower, but complete.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_get_business
tools.description: Get full detail for one business: currency, address, type, and settings.

business_id.description: Business to operate on: the base64 id from wave_list_businesses (a bare business UUID is also accepted). Defaults to the business set by wave_set_default_business. When calls may be minutes apart, pass it on every call.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_set_default_business
tools.description: Set the business that later tool calls use when none is given. This is connector state, not a change in Wave. The hosted connector keeps it for the authenticated connection (legacy clients: the session); the local server keeps it until it restarts (set WAVE_BUSINESS_ID to make it permanent). Passing business_id explicitly always overrides it.

business_id.description: The Wave business ID to make the default: the base64 id from wave_list_businesses, or the bare business UUID.

tools.name: wave_get_invoice_estimate_settings
tools.description: Get the branding applied to invoices and estimates: accent color and logo.

business_id.description: Business to operate on: the base64 id from wave_list_businesses (a bare business UUID is also accepted). Defaults to the business set by wave_set_default_business. When calls may be minutes apart, pass it on every call.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

tools.name: wave_list_accounts
tools.description: List the chart of accounts, with balances. Filter by type to find the account a transaction needs: EXPENSE for expense categories, INCOME for revenue, ASSET with subtype CASH_AND_BANK for bank accounts, LIABILITY with subtype CREDIT_CARD for cards.

business_id.description: Business to operate on: the base64 id from wave_list_businesses (a bare business UUID is also accepted). Defaults to the business set by wave_set_default_business. When calls may be minutes apart, pass it on every call.

types.description: Filter by type: ASSET, LIABILITY, EQUITY, INCOME, EXPENSE.

is_archived.description: Filter to archived (true) or active (false) accounts.

fetch_all.description: Walk every page instead of returning just one. Slower, but complete.

response_format.description: Output format: "markdown" for a compact human-readable summary, "json" for the complete record.

email.description: Exact email match, applied by Wave.

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring match on name, applied locally.

sort.description: NAME_ASC, NAME_DESC, CREATED_AT_ASC/DESC, MODIFIED_AT_ASC/DESC. Defaults to NAME_ASC.

modified_after.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only customers changed after it.

modified_before.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only customers changed before it.

instructions:
Tools for Wave Accounting (waveapps.com) covering the full public GraphQL API:
businesses, chart of accounts, customers, vendors, products, sales taxes,
invoices and invoice payments, estimates and deposit payments, and money
(bookkeeping) transactions.

Most tools operate on one business. Call wave_list_businesses first, then
wave_set_default_business so later calls can omit business_id. Any tool still
accepts an explicit business_id to override the default. Business ids are the
base64 ids that wave_list_businesses returns; a bare business UUID is also accepted.

Every read tool accepts response_format ("markdown" for a compact summary,
"json" for the complete record) and paginates with page/page_size, or
fetch_all=true to walk every page.

Wave has no query for money transactions: they can be created but not read
back. Vendors are read-only. Invoice and estimate line items must each
reference a product.
